# a11y.skip-link — Page has navigation before the main content but no working skip link

- **Check ID:** `a11y.skip-link`
- **Default severity:** `warning`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 2.4.1
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/a11y.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/a11y.skip-link.md`](../a11y.skip-link.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

A page puts navigation before its main content and has no working "skip to content" link.

## Why it matters

Keyboard and screen reader users reach each page by moving through its links one at a time. If the header and menu come first, they must move through all of them on every page before they get to the content. A skip link, the first link on the page, jumps past the repeated block. It is usually hidden until it receives focus. This is the classic way to meet the "bypass blocks" requirement.

## What it checks

Pages that have a visible `<main>` (or `role="main"`), a `<nav>` or `role="navigation"` before it, and at least 3 links before it. For those pages, one of the first two links on the page must be a skip link: an in-page link (`href="#something"`) whose target exists and is the main content, inside it, or a wrapper that contains it. Pages with fewer than 3 links before the content are not reported, because there is little to skip. A missing `<main>` is reported by [`a11y.landmarks`](a11y.landmarks.md).

When an early link looks like a skip link (its text or `aria-label` says skip, jump, main, or content) but its target is missing or outside the content, the report says so instead of "no skip link".

## How to fix

```html
<body>
  <a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
  <nav>...</nav>
  <main id="main">...</main>
</body>
```

```css
.skip-link { position: absolute; left: -9999px; }
.skip-link:focus { left: 1rem; top: 1rem; z-index: 10; }
```

Put it first so it is the first thing a keyboard user reaches, and make it visible on focus. There is no automatic edit, because it also needs a style rule and an id on `<main>`.

## Options

None.

## Standards

- [WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/bypass-blocks.html)
- [Technique G1: Adding a link at the top of each page that goes directly to the main content area](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G1)
